newsitem.title: CHINA: China parliament mulls anti-corruption body.
newsitem.headline: China parliament mulls anti-corruption body.

text.p: China's parliament is considering the creation of a supervisory body to boost government efficiency and curb corruption, the China Daily said on Wednesday.

The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress would review the draft Law on Supervision of Government Staff during its current session, the official newspaper quoted parliamentary chief Qiao Shi as saying.
"Under the draft law, a new body will supervise all governmental departments, civil servants and staff appointed to governmental departments," the newspaper said.
"Any other administrative departments, social organisations or individuals will not be allowed to intervene in the supervisory body's working."

It gave no details of how the oversight body would be organised, but it said those who violated codes of conduct would be fined, demoted or dismissed. Those who acquired illegal properties would be fined or have them confiscated.
China has struggled to curb rising corruption among officials who use their bureaucratic clout to amass wealth and whose powerful connections make them difficult to prosecute.
Analysts say parliamentary chief Qiao is eager to expand the influence of the National People's Congress, long seen as a rubber-stamp for the ruling Communist Party headed by Jiang Zemin.
